interest: Tsingtao Japanese residents used an alleged flag insult during a 1936 customs seizure to agitate for intervention.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.015393) covers an international controversy in June through October 1936 arising from the Chinese Maritime Customs' interception and firing upon a Japanese vessel off Tsingtao (Qingdao), China. Japanese residents and a local Japanese federation alleged that Chinese customs officers had insulted the Japanese national flag during the vessel's seizure, leading to tense mass protest meetings in Tsingtao that American diplomats warned were intended to provoke Japanese armed intervention. The file comprises State Department cross-reference sheets and an original diplomatic telegram from the American Embassy in Peiping relaying reports from the American Consulate in Tsingtao, documenting the initial confrontation in late June 1936 through to the reported terms of settlement reached between Japanese and Chinese authorities in October 1936.
